persona: Food scientist running a shelf-life stability study on fresh orange juice, tracking titratable acidity (% citric acid) of the same bottles over 21 days at three storage temperatures.
source_style: hand-maintained lab tracking spreadsheet, one row per bottle, exported to CSV for sharing

columns.name: Bottle_ID
columns.notes: Unique bottle identifier B1-B9, 3 bottles per temperature

columns.name: Storage_Temp_C
columns.notes: Storage temperature in Celsius: 4, 25, or 37; only 3 fixed levels despite being numeric-looking, and row 2 repeats the unit 'C' as a fake data value

columns.name: Day_0
columns.notes: Titratable acidity (% citric acid, w/v) measured at day 0

columns.name: Day_21
columns.notes: Titratable acidity (%) at day 21; blank for bottle B8, which spoiled before that reading was taken

columns.name: Notes
columns.notes: Free text, blank for all rows except B8, which explains the missing Day_21 value

clean_table.Notes: visible fermentation at day 21, sample discarded

intended_analysis: Repeated-measures / mixed-model ANOVA of titratable acidity on Storage_Temp_C and Day (time), using Bottle_ID as the repeated-measures unit, to test whether acidity declines faster at higher storage temperatures over the 21-day period; B8's missing Day_21 reading should be excluded (or modeled as missing), not imputed as zero.
mess_applied: Wide (one row per bottle, one column per timepoint) rather than tidy long format — needs reshaping to long form (Bottle_ID, Day, TA_pct) before a repeated-measures model can be fit
A units row immediately under the header (row 2: '', 'C', '%', '%', '%', '%', '') that is not a data row and must be skipped, not parsed as bottle B0
Storage_Temp_C looks purely numeric but is really a 3-level categorical factor (only 4, 25, 37 occur) — a naive reader may treat it as continuous
One genuinely missing value (B8, Day_21) represented as an empty CSV field, explained only in the free-text Notes column, not by a sentinel like NA or -999

Trailing zeros are lost on export: two cells that were measured/recorded as 1.00 (B1 Day_14, B4 Day_0) appear in the file as '1.0' while every other value keeps 2 decimal places, so decimal-place count is not a reliable signal of precision
what_a_naive_reader_would_get_wrong: Reading row 2 as the first data row would inject a fake 'bottle' with Storage_Temp_C='C' (text) and TA values of '%' into the dataset; and treating Storage_Temp_C as a continuous numeric predictor (rather than 3 fixed levels) would turn a one-way/factorial design into a spurious linear-regression-on-temperature analysis.
